--- title: "Boundary vintages" jupyter: coi-docs --- County and tract boundaries change: counties split, merge, or get replaced entirely. A FIPS code without a vintage is an assembly name without a patch level — the same code can mean a different shape depending on when it was issued. ## The worked example: SVI's own county count CDC/ATSDR's Social Vulnerability Index republishes the whole country every edition, so its county count across editions is a direct, queryable record of every boundary change that mattered at the county level between 2014 and 2022: ::: {#2758d1b1 .cell execution_count=1} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ```{=html}
svi_edition counties
0 2014 3142
1 2016 3142
2 2018 3142
3 2020 3143
4 2022 3144
``` ::: ::: 3,142 / 3,142 / 3,142 / 3,143 / 3,144 — flat for three editions, then +1, then +1 again. Both jumps are real redistrictings, not data errors, and both are queryable directly: ::: {#4bb02d57 .cell execution_count=2} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ```{=html}
svi_edition rows
0 2014 1
1 2016 1
2 2018 1
3 2020 2
4 2022 2
``` ::: ::: Alaska's Valdez-Cordova Census Area (`02261`) splits into Chugach (`02063`) and Copper River (`02066`) starting with the 2020 edition — one row becomes two, the +1 between the 2018 and 2020 counts. ::: {#b9614615 .cell execution_count=3} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ```{=html}
svi_edition rows
0 2014 8
1 2016 8
2 2018 8
3 2020 8
4 2022 9
``` ::: ::: Connecticut's eight legacy counties persist through the 2020 edition; the nine 2022-vintage planning regions arrive with the 2022 edition — the +1 between the 2020 and 2022 counts. The third real change in this window — South Dakota's Shannon County becoming Oglala Lakota County in 2015 — is a rename-and-recode, not a boundary change, so it doesn't move the county *count* at all; it shows up instead as `fips` changing from `46113` to `46102` starting with the 2016 edition, with the pre-2016 code still resolving through `geography.alias`: ::: {#f6e395b8 .cell execution_count=4} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ```{=html}
old_geo_id new_geo_id effective_year change_type old_name new_name
0 county:46113 county:46102 2015 recode_and_rename Shannon County Oglala Lakota County
``` ::: ::: ## Why `geography.unit` carries a `vintage` at all Every fact in the lake joins through `geography.unit` by `geo_id`, but a `geo_id` alone doesn't say which boundary edition it belongs to. `vintage` makes that explicit, and it's why every recipe on this site names a vintage on its geography join (`u.vintage = 2026`) instead of trusting a measure's own `geo_vintage` column — see [Time axes](time-axes.qmd) and [cancer-on-ice#21](https://github.com/seandavi/cancer-on-ice/issues/21) for the open question that makes this necessary today. `geography.alias` resolves an old code that was renamed or recoded (not reshaped) to its current one, so a join on a retired code still finds its record instead of silently dropping it. [Recipes › A county's boundary history](/recipes/boundary-history.qmd) runs Connecticut's own boundary history live, in your browser.
